answer: Require every agent to lock a refundable stake before it can earn, like copper wiring that only carries current once bonded. One identity is cheap, but thousands each lock capital, and that stake is slashed if duplicate behaviour is proven. A new agent must cross a canyon of checks — a unique device, a record of completed work, a vouch from an established peer — before its quota grows, while a swarm chasing the same nectar of rewards stays throttled. Forging scale then costs real money and time, not just new names.
